extracted.intended_audience: market participants, exchange members and affiliates, data vendors/subscribers, brokers/dealers, and members of the public who may submit comments on SEC SRO rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for self-regulatory-organization (SRO) proposed rule changes and for submitting public comments to the SEC (e.g., market-data product and fee filings). Covers statutory-consistency tests, competition/burden considerations, product-content/availability expectations, and procedural rules for comment submission and Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable and not unfairly discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes that the proposed discount is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply equally to all Trading Permit Holders and non-Trading Permit Holders who purchase historical Open-Close Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: equal application of discount to all purchasers (TPHs and non-TPHs) supports claim of non-discrimination; used by Exchange to justify rule change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchase is discretionary, not compulsory
rubrics_metrics.description: The purchase of this data product is discretionary and not compulsory. Indeed, no market participant is required to purchase the historical Open-Close Data, and the Exchange is not required to make the historical Open-Close Data available to all investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: emphasizing optional nature of product supports arguments that measures do not burden competition or coerce buyers; potential purchasers may request data or decline purchase at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unnecessary or inappropriate burden on competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a statutory-standard check: evaluate whether a rule change imposes burdens on competition beyond those necessary to further the Act’s purposes; exchanges argue market contestability and freedom to respond reduce any such burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive environment and freedom to modify fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange operates in a highly competitive environment in which the Exchange must continually adjust its fees to remain competitive. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees in response, including the adoption of similar discounts to those fees, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee changes... may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: existence of competing exchanges and ability to change fees is a factor in assessing competitive impact of a filing; commenters and Commission may consider whether competitors can and will respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of close substitutes (direct competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-Close Data is subject to direct competition from several other options exchanges that offer substitutes to Open-Close Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: presence of substitute products (other exchanges’ data, consolidated feeds) is used to justify non-discriminatory effect and limited competitive burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit conditional on meeting minimum purchase amount
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes that this does not impose any burden on intramarket competition as the benefit is given to any purchasers who meet the minimum purchase amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: equitable application of benefits to purchasers meeting objective thresholds (minimum purchase amount) is offered to rebut intramarket discrimination claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permits fair competition among national securities exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes this proposed rule change permits fair competition among national securities exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: filings commonly assert that product/fee changes will enhance the Exchange’s ability to compete and thus are pro-competitive; the Commission evaluates such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of comments should address statutory consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for commenters: explicitly address whether and how the proposal is (or is not) consistent with the securities laws and the Act when submitting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and formats for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted by the Commission’s internet comment form; or send an email to rule-comments@sec.gov (include file number on subject line); or send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, SEC. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instructions: include the file number (e.g., SR-CBOE-2025-035) in subject line; use a single submission method; paper in triplicate if using mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and availability of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will post all comments on the Commission’s internet website. Copies of the submission, all subsequent amendments, and all written communications relating to the proposed rule change... will be available for website viewing and printing in the Commission’s Public Reference Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: commenters should presume submissions will be publicly posted and made available for inspection; see Public Reference Room access hours and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include personally identifiable information (PII) in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit privacy guidance: exclude PII you don’t want public; Commission may redact or withhold obscene/copyrighted material under 5 U.S.C. 552.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and deadline for comments; Commission’s 60-day authority
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should refer to file number SR-... and should be submitted on or before [date]. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: respect published comment deadlines; be aware of Commission’s 60-day review window and grounds for temporary suspension (public interest/protection of investors/purposes of Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b) and Section 6(b)(5) objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular being designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination..., to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination among customers, brokers, or dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive legal standard the Exchange must address in its filing and that commenters/Commission will evaluate: fraud prevention, fairness, market efficiency, investor protection, and non-discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-content expectation: inclusion of Auction Imbalance Information
rubrics_metrics.description: An enhanced NYSE Texas Integrated Feed would include Auction Imbalance Information: real-time order imbalances that accumulate prior to the opening, prior to any re-opening auction after a halt, and prior to the close. Auction Imbalance Information includes Total Imbalance, Market Imbalance, Indicative Match Price and Matched Volume (as defined in Exchange rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: defines the concrete data elements and markets events that an integrated feed enhancement should include; useful for evaluating whether proposed product content meets market needs and is consistent with peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product availability on equivalent basis / no charge (non-discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The enhanced product would be available to all of the Exchange’s vendors and subscribers on an equivalent basis at no cost as the Exchange currently does not charge a fee for subscribing to the NYSE Texas Integrated Feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: providing the product to all vendors/subscribers equivalently (and at stated cost) is a factor supporting non-discrimination claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of alternatives reduces claims of unreasonable discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence of alternatives to the Exchange’s product, including real-time consolidated data, free delayed consolidated data, and proprietary data from other sources, ensures that the Exchange is not unreasonably discriminatory because vendors and subscribers can elect these alternatives as their individual business cases warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: assessment of alleged discrimination should consider availability and adequacy of substitute data sources for market participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for filing under Rule 19b-4(f)(6) (immediate effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6) normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after filing. Rule 19b-4(f)(6) requires that the filing (i) does not significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) does not impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) does not become operative prior to 30 days (or shorter time designated by Commission). It also requires prior written notice to the Commission at least five business days before filing (or shorter time if designated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: exchanges may rely on this pathway only when meeting the three-prong test; waiver of the 30-day operative delay may be requested and considered consistent with investor protection/public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission’s waiver of operative delay if consistent with investor protection/public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may designate a shorter time (waive the 30-day operative delay) if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: exchanges may request waiver to implement technical changes sooner; Commission balances speed against investor protection in deciding waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must be reasonable and equitably allocated (Section 6(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act, which requires that Exchange rules provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: justification for fee changes should address reasonableness and equitable allocation among members/users; comparison to peer exchanges and explanation of benefits/service quality are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of market comparators and economic indices to justify fees (PPI/Data PPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange supports its proposed fee increase by comparing to competitor fee levels (Nasdaq, NYSE, MIAX Pearl) and by noting that 10 Gb physical port fees have been static in nominal terms since 2018 and therefore falling in real terms due to inflation; it cites the Producer Price Index (Data PPI) and NAICS 518210 as measures of relevant price changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: exchanges can (and do) rely on market comparator pricing and industry-specific PPIs to justify increases; commenters may contest comparator choice or inflation measure relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundling/single-fee treatment across affiliated exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: A single 10 Gb physical port can be used to access the Systems of affiliated exchanges, and only one monthly fee currently (and will continue) to apply per 10 Gb physical port regardless of how many affiliated exchanges are accessed through that one port.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: bundling and single-fee policies for multi-exchange access are relevant to reasonableness and equitable-allocation analyses; compare to other exchange groups that charge per affiliated exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing must include statements of purpose, statutory basis, and comments received
rubrics_metrics.description: In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: filings should contain explanatory statements of purpose and statutory basis and discuss any member/participant comments; these form the basis for Commission and public review.
